mechanism: Normalize CiATR.Main to price: norm_vol = atr_val / bid. Skip all entries when norm_vol > InpMaxChopPct (default 0.006, too choppy) or norm_vol < InpMinVolPct (default 0.0005, too quiet). ATR also scales SL distance (ATR×InpATRstopMult) and risk-based lot sizing (risk_amount / loss_per_lot).
data_needed: CiATR on chart symbol/TF; bid/ask; MaxChopPct and MinVolPct thresholds; ATR stop multiplier; account balance and tick value/size for sizing.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: GBPUSD; tested M30 (noisy) vs H4 (clearer trends); ATR period 14; fast EMA 8 / slow EMA 34
why_new_for_mis: Turns ATR/price into an explicit two-sided volatility admission gate (chop vs dead) before trend logic—MIS can tag untradeable vol regimes separately from directional state.

mechanism: Two CiMA EMAs define directional regime: uptrend if fast>slow, downtrend if fast<slow. Entry only when |price−fastMA| ≤ InpPullbackFactor×ATR inside that regime—pullback-to-fast-MA as the actionable state within the MA trend.
data_needed: CiMA fast/slow (EMA close); CiATR; pullback factor; prefer Main(1) for non-repainting bar-close decisions.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: GBPUSD; M30 vs H4 Strategy Tester; fast 8 / slow 34 EMA
why_new_for_mis: Couples a binary MA trend regime with an ATR-scaled distance-to-fast-MA proximity sensor—MIS can report trend state and pullback depth as joint regime coordinates.

mechanism: Walkthrough of integrating CPanel, CChartObjectLabel, and CPicture into a static chart InfoPanel EA (include/declare/Create/configure/cleanup). No market regime, volatility, liquidity, or sequence sensing is built.

mechanism: On each new bar, least-squares fit close vs bar index over PeriodBars; median = a·(n−1)+b at newest completed bar; residual σ = sqrt(Σe²/(n−2)); bands = median ± Deviation·σ. UseMeanReversion: buy bounce off lower (prevLow≤lower, bid>lower) / sell bounce off upper; else breakout: ask>upper buy / bid<lower sell. Numeric model is authoritative vs optional CChartObjectStdDevChannel viz.
data_needed: CopyRates closes; PeriodBars (default 50); Deviation k (default 2); completed-bar IsNewBar trigger; bid/ask.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: _Symbol PERIOD_CURRENT; Strategy Tester visual; Deviation=2, PeriodBars=50
why_new_for_mis: Residual-σ around a rolling linear-regression centerline is a volatility envelope that also flips between mean-reversion and breakout modes—MIS can sense band width and price-vs-band state as a joint vol/structure sensor.

mechanism: CMyCandlePatternSignal: detect Doji (body≤range·threshold), bullish/bearish engulfing (body≥prev·ratio), hammer/shooting-star geometry, morning/evening star; LongCondition/ShortCondition sum pattern weights (e.g. engulfing 80, hammer 70, doji 60, morning star 90) when IS_PATTERN_USAGE enabled; Wizard opens when aggregate votes ≥ Signal_ThresholdOpen.
data_needed: OHLC series via m_open/high/low/close; per-pattern weights; doji_threshold; engulfing_ratio; Wizard open/close thresholds.

why_new_for_mis: Maps discrete candle morphologies into a calibrated 0–100 confidence vote—MIS can treat pattern-class scores as a price-action microstructure sensor rather than binary pattern flags.
quote: Using a weighted voting system, each pattern contributes its confidence level to the final decision, with the total needing to exceed the Wizard's threshold for a trade to execute.

mechanism: Find swing high/low over m_depth via iHighest/iLowest; compute Fib levels 0.236/0.382/0.500/0.618/0.786 from range with trend-aware direction; classify touch into pattern tiers (0.382/0.618→strong pattern0, 0.500→medium pattern1, 0.236/0.786→weak pattern2) within price tolerance; boost to pattern3 when bullish/bearish PA confirmation (engulfing/hammer) coincides.
data_needed: Swing depth; min/max retracement; level tolerance in points; OHLC for PA confirm; pattern weights 0–100.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: USDJPY M5 Fibonacci-only test; Multi-Signal Expert also EURUSD M5 with Fib+AC+MA+RSI
why_new_for_mis: Structures Fib touches as strength-tiered sensors with optional PA confluence upgrade—MIS can score proximity to structurally strong vs weak retracement levels, not a single Fib hit flag.
quote: The 0.382 and 0.618 levels are considered the "golden" Fibonacci retracements and get the highest weight (pattern 0), while the 0.500 level is psychologically important but mathematically less significant (pattern 1).

mechanism: Wizard CExpertSignal aggregates filters (Fib primary, MA trend context, RSI momentum, AC energy) each casting 0–100 confidence×module weight; trade only if sum ≥ ThresholdOpen. Article argues assigning triggers vs filters and raising thresholds so weak modules cannot open alone—collective vote as adaptive multi-strategy regime when different modules dominate across conditions.
data_needed: Per-module Long/ShortCondition scores; module weights; open/close thresholds; optional confluence bonus.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD M5 Multi-Signal Expert; Fib+AC+MA+RSI; default equal weights=1.0 critiqued
why_new_for_mis: Frames a team of heterogeneous signals with explicit trigger/filter roles and a confidence threshold as a multi-strategy regime sensor—MIS can track which module family is currently dominating the vote.
quote: When a trending market shifts to a range, your trend-following signals may grow quiet, but your mean-reversion or oscillator-based signals can pick up the slack. The EA doesn't need to be rewritten; it naturally leans on the strategies that are currently working.

mechanism: IsTradingTime() maps broker clock to minute-of-day vs Session_Start/End (handles midnight wrap); CanOpenNewTrade() also enforces MaxTradesPerSession via history/open-position count reset each session. OnTick only calls ExtExpert.OnTick when gates pass—otherwise blocks new entries (optional Close_Outside_Session). Structural fix for unconstrained multi-signal overtrading across unsuitable hours.
data_needed: Broker TimeCurrent; session HH:MM bounds; MaxTradesPerSession; session trade counter from history deals.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Multi-Signal Expert (Fib/AC/MA/RSI); example journal window ~00:30–06:05 EURUSD; session e.g. 09:00–17:00
why_new_for_mis: Treats clock session and per-session trade quota as first-class regime gates that govern when signal votes may act—MIS can mark session-admissible vs blocked execution regimes independent of indicator state.
quote: Meaningful optimization focuses on controlling when signals are permitted to participate in decision-making, how frequently they are allowed to trigger trade actions, and under which market regimes their interpretations remain valid.

mechanism: ALGLIB CSSAModel on last LookbackBars closes: SSASetWindow + SSASetAlgoTopKRealtime(rank) + SSAAnalyzeLast → trend vs noise. Compare baseline EMA cross arrows on raw price vs EMA-cross on FilterSMA/EMA/LRMA-preprocessed series; SSA trend stays flatter in sideways markets, cutting whipsaw crosses while preserving trend crosses.

quote: In sideways or choppy periods... The blue arrows will fire repeatedly... The red arrows, however, will be much sparser... Notice how the SSA line (magenta) behaves. During flat periods, it often becomes nearly horizontal, refusing to generate crossovers.

mechanism: Spline1DBuildCubic on (bar_index, close) over lookback; Spline1DDiff yields first derivative at each point; plot close + scale·deriv. Zero-crossings / sign of derivative mark directional momentum shifts, often leading EMA crosses.
data_needed: Lookback closes; cubic spline interpolant; SplineDerivScale for display; optional zero-cross detector on deriv.
why_new_for_mis: Instantaneous spline slope as an early momentum-change sensor distinct from lagging MA crosses—MIS can flag derivative sign flips as regime-change candidates.
quote: The first derivative represents the instantaneous rate of change. Zero-crossings of the derivative can indicate directional shifts.

mechanism: ALGLIB PolynomialFit degree d over InpPeriod prices (x=0..N−1); evaluate middle at x=N−1 via BarycentricCalc; unbiased residual σ = sqrt(Σresid²/(N−d−1)); Upper/Lower = middle ± InpDeviation·σ. Bands widen/tighten with residual volatility around the curved trend.
data_needed: Applied price series; InpDegree; InpPeriod; InpDeviation; ALGLIB PolynomialFit/BarycentricCalc.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1 defaults degree=2, period=20, deviation=2.0; any symbol/TF
why_new_for_mis: Volatility bands referenced to a curved polynomial trend (not SMA/linear) so envelope width tracks residual noise around accelerating/S-shaped structure—MIS gets curvature-aware vol envelopes.
quote: This standard deviation is conceptually similar to what Bollinger Bands use, but with an important difference: the reference point is a curved regression line rather than a simple moving average. The bands therefore adapt not only to changes in volatility but also to changes in the shape of the trend itself.

mechanism: Interpret fitted polynomial centerline: slope → up/down trend direction; curvature (degree≥2 bend, degree≥3 inflection) → acceleration vs deceleration / S-turn; expanding vs contracting bandwidth → rising vs falling residual vol. Degree/period trade off flexibility vs overfitting.
data_needed: Polynomial coefficients or successive middle values for slope/Δslope; band width = upper−lower over time.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1; degree 1 baseline vs 2–3 on parabolic moves; period 10 vs 50 experiments
why_new_for_mis: Elevates slope+curvature+bandwidth of a poly channel into an explicit multi-aspect regime state (direction, acceleration, vol envelope)—beyond linear-channel tilt alone.
quote: The slope of the center line indicates the direction of the trend... The curvature of this line reveals whether the trend is accelerating (becoming steeper) or decelerating (flattening out)... expanding bands indicate increasing volatility, while contracting bands suggest consolidation

mechanism: For each symbol×timeframe cell over m_windowSize closes: T=OLS slope, M=last−first price change, V=Std(prices); raw = w_t·T + w_m·M − w_v·V; S = raw·scaleFactor (~[−100,+100]). Color maps sign/intensity; same-color row across TFs = higher-probability aligned regime; mixed colors = caution. Timer refresh with differential cell updates.
data_needed: CopyClose per symbol/TF; window≥5; weights (default 0.4/0.3/0.3); scaleFactor; symbol and TF lists.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Default EURUSD,GBPUSD,USDJPY,AUDUSD,USDCAD,NZDUSD × M5,M15,H1,H4,D1; live NZDUSD M15; window=50
why_new_for_mis: Single comparable multi-TF composite that explicitly subtracts volatility from trend+momentum—MIS can read cross-TF color concordance as a confluence regime grid, not isolated per-TF indicators.
quote:
we compute a composite score S over a rolling window... T = linear trend slope... M = momentum... V = volatility = standard deviation of prices
We then multiply by m_scaleFactor... Why subtract volatility? High volatility often accompanies uncertainty; reducing the score in such regimes acts as a penalty

mechanism: Each new bar, CNlEq Levenberg–Marquardt fits p=[β1,β2,γ] on WindowSize closes: logistic(β)→α; adapt=α·(1+γ·|Δprice|) capped at 0.99 drives dual EWMAs; residual = price−0.5·(ema1+ema2). Signal when filter vs its 10-bar MA; SL distance = ATR·clamp(γ). Online re-fit adapts threshold/alphas as volatility regimes shift.
data_needed: Rolling close window (default 50); ATR(14); CNlEq LM state + residuals/Jacobian; DefaultGamma fallback; RiskRewardRatio.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: GBPUSD H1; WindowSize=50; MaxIterations=30; tested 2023 and visual 2024 segments
why_new_for_mis: Volatility-scaled EWMA alphas and γ-threshold re-estimated each bar by LM turn a static MA cross into an online vol-regime-adaptive filter—MIS can track γ/α as live regime parameters, not fixed inputs.
quote: Financial markets exhibit nonstationarity: volatility clusters, trend reversals, and liquidity shifts create distinct regimes... The solver adjusts the crossover threshold in real time using a volatility estimate such as the Average True Range (ATR).
